Consult Summary:
- Postpartum patient (4 weeks post–C-section) with acute onset shortness of breath at rest and new non-productive cough; clinician concerned for venous thromboembolism/pulmonary embolism; advised urgent hospital evaluation.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden shortness of breath beginning about 1 hour prior to call while sitting and watching TV.
- Timeline:
  - Cough began yesterday; non-productive.
  - Shortness of breath started acutely over the last hour.
  - Cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
- Symptom details:
  - Shortness of breath at rest; patient feels heart “racing.”
  - No chest pain reported.
  - Chest soreness with deep inspiration; C-section scar tender.
  - No prior similar episodes.
- Triggers/relievers: Not documented.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Palpitations/anxiety noted.
  - No sputum production.
- Systems review (pertinent negatives/positives):
  - Baby well; no cough/cold symptoms in infant.
  - No other systemic symptoms documented.

Past Medical History:
- Postpartum status, 4 weeks after cesarean section.
- No other medical problems reported.
- Medications:
  - Codeine for post–C-section pain; used fairly regularly but not taken for about 1 week (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies:
  - Ibuprofen; reaction details not described.

Social History:
- Lives with partner (partner at work during call).
- At home alone with newborn during consult; plans to self-transport to hospital with baby and supplies.
- Tobacco, alcohol, and substance use: not documented.

Family History:
- Mother with history of leg clots (DVT).

Physical Examination:
- Not documented (telehealth visit; no vitals recorded).

Investigations:
- Telehealth pulse check: patient counted 30 beats during a brief timed interval (duration not documented); clinician interpreted heart rate as “slightly fast.”

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute shortness of breath in a postpartum patient (4 weeks post–C-section); tachycardia; concern for venous thromboembolism/pulmonary embolism.
  - Advised immediate evaluation at the hospital.
  - Discussed ambulance vs self-transport; patient declined ambulance and will self-transport promptly with baby and necessary items.
  - Advised to avoid taking codeine for now.
  - Education provided: postpartum clots can occur in legs or lungs; treatable; needs hospital assessment and management.
- Issue 2: New non-productive cough (onset yesterday).
  - To be evaluated at hospital as part of workup for acute shortness of breath.
- Issue 3: Ibuprofen allergy.
  - Documented; reaction details unknown.

General plan items:
- No additional management documented beyond urgent hospital evaluation.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: comprehensive vitals; full ROS; detailed past medical/surgical history; obstetric/postpartum course; leg symptoms (pain/swelling); smoking/alcohol/substance use; full medication reconciliation with doses/routes/frequencies; immunization status; breastfeeding status.
- Internal conflicts: Date of birth stated as April 20, 1980; clinician subsequently said 1983—conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor pauses and brief unclear segments without impact on clinical content.
